entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Lamia bint Majed Al Saud is a Saudi royal who serves as the Secretary General of Alwaleed Philanthropies, a prominent charitable organization founded by Prince Alwaleed bin Talal Al Saud in 1977. Born into the Saudi royal family, Lamia has been instrumental in promoting the philanthropic efforts of her family, particularly in the areas of education and healthcare. As a member of the Saudi royal family, she has played a significant role in shaping the country's social and cultural landscape, often in collaboration with international partners. Her work has been influenced by the 2015 Paris Agreement on climate change and the subsequent Saudi Vision 2030 initiative. Through her philanthropic efforts, Lamia has aimed to promote women's empowerment and education, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa. Her work has been recognized globally, and she has been named a Forbes 100 Most Powerful Women in the World in 2020. Despite the complexities of her role, Lamia remains a prominent figure in Saudi society, using her influence to promote positive change and address pressing global issues.
